title: GDPR privacy (add-on)
description: A GDPR programme on the Core registers and the GDPR requirement library. Adds records of processing, data subject requests with their deadline, personal data breaches with the 72-hour clock, DPIAs and (under Suppliers) processors and DPAs; Full adds transfers outside the EEA, the retention schedule and consent records. On the shared registers it adds the Privacy risk category, links from risks to processing and DPIAs, the "Personal data breach" incident type that opens a breach record, example privacy documents and a GDPR view on each. Retention rules ship as suggestions. Installs the Core registers first when they are missing. Own words throughout; article headings are the official ones.

levels.description: Everything in Starter plus transfers outside the EEA, the retention schedule and consent records.

sheets.name: Records of processing

fields.description: Why you use the data, in a sentence a member of the public would understand.

fields.name: Legitimate interests assessment
fields.description: Only for legitimate interests: the interest, why the processing is needed and why it does not override the people's rights.

fields.name: Condition for special categories
fields.description: Only when health, biometric, beliefs or other special categories are used: the condition you rely on.

fields.name: Recipients
fields.description: Who receives the data: teams, processors, authorities, other organisations.

fields.name: How long we keep it
fields.description: The period in words, e.g. "6 years after the tax year". The retention schedule (Full) holds the detail.

fields.name: Security measures
fields.description: A general description of the technical and organisational measures that protect this data.

rules.message: Add the purpose, the lawful basis and the business owner before approving.

fields.name: Approval step
fields.description: Where the record is in its approval. Set by the approval workflow, never by hand.

sheets.name: Retention schedule
sheets.description: How long you keep each kind of record and why. The schedule says the policy; the retention rules in each sheet's settings (Sheet settings › Retention) apply it: due records go to Workspace admin › Retention, where an owner or admin approves the erasure. Periods shipped here are suggestions: set your own.

fields.name: Applied by
fields.description: The sheet and its retention rule that apply this period, or how it is done elsewhere.

sheets.name: Consent records
sheets.description: Proof of consent where consent is your lawful basis: who agreed, to what, when, how and with which wording, and when they withdrew. Withdrawing must be as easy as giving consent.

fields.name: Wording version

rules.name: Consent: 2 years after withdrawal
rules.note: A suggestion, not advice: keep proof as long as you may need to show the consent was valid, then erase.

values.likelihood_scale: 1 Rare: no sign it could happen with the measures in place. 2 Unlikely: has happened elsewhere. 3 Possible: has happened here or to a similar organisation. 4 Likely: expected within a year. 5 Almost certain: happening now or several times a year.
values.impact_scale: 1 Negligible: people are not affected or only briefly inconvenienced. 2 Minor: small inconvenience they get over easily. 3 Moderate: real problems for some people, such as costs or stress. 4 Major: serious harm such as fraud, discrimination or loss of a job. 5 Severe: lasting or irreversible harm to many people, or to vulnerable people.

automations.name: Request deadline in 7 days → tell the handler

actions.message: {id} {request_type} request is due on {deadline}. Answer it, or extend it now if it is complex and tell the person why.

automations.description: SLA clock, step 1: seven days before a request’s deadline (one month from receipt, plus any extension), the handler is reminded to answer or to extend in time.

automations.name: Request past its deadline → escalate to the DPO and top management

actions.message: {id} {request_type} request was due on {deadline} and is not closed. The person may complain to the supervisory authority: answer now.

automations.description: Escalation ladder, step 2: a request still open the day after its deadline goes to the handler, the data protection officer and top management, because a late answer is a breach of the person’s rights.

automations.name: New request from the form → tell the DPO
Breach: 48 hours left on the 72-hour clock → tell the lead and the DPO

actions.message: {id} {name}: 48 hours left to report to the supervisory authority. Assess the risk and decide now.

automations.description: SLA clock: 24 hours after you became aware, unless you decided not to report, the breach lead and the DPO are told that 48 hours are left to report to the supervisory authority.

automations.name: Breach: 12 hours left → escalate to top management

actions.message: {id} {name}: 12 hours left to report to the supervisory authority. Report what you know now; you may add the rest later.

automations.description: Escalation: with 12 hours left on the 72-hour clock, top management joins the lead and the DPO, so the report goes out in time even when details are missing.

automations.name: Breach reported through the form → tell the DPO

actions.message: New breach report {id}: {name}. The 72-hour clock runs from {aware_at}.

automations.name: Breach assessed as high risk → tell the lead and the DPO

actions.message: {id} {name} is high risk: tell the people affected without undue delay unless an exception applies, and record why.

automations.name: DPA review in 30 days → tell the owner

actions.message: {id} {name}: review the DPA, the sub-processors and any transfers by {next_review}.

automations.name: Breach decided not reportable → ask the DPO to sign off the decision
automations.description: Gate: deciding not to report a breach to the authority sends the decision and its reasons to the DPO for sign-off (12-hour limit), so the decision is never one person’s alone and the reasons are kept.

automations.name: Processing needs a DPIA → open a linked DPIA
automations.description: Cascade: marking a processing record "DPIA needed" opens a draft DPIA linked to it, so high-risk processing cannot start without an assessment on record.

automations.name: Processing record approved → set the next review in a year
automations.description: Recurring review: each time a record of processing is approved, its next review is set a year ahead, and the review reminder below asks the business owner to check it again then.

automations.name: Processing review in 30 days → ask the business owner

actions.message: Check {id} {name} by {next_review}: purpose, lawful basis, recipients, retention and security still as recorded? Then submit it for approval again.

automations.name: DPIA review in 30 days → tell the owner

actions.message: {id} {name} is due for review on {next_review}. Check that the processing and the risks have not changed.

setup.title: GDPR setup
setup.description: Eight steps to a privacy programme you can show to a supervisory authority. Each step’s progress comes from your sheets. Give a member the job title "Data protection officer" so alerts and approvals reach them.

steps.title: Record your processing
steps.body: List each purpose for which you use personal data, with the lawful basis, whose data it is, who receives it and a business owner. Approve each record.

steps.title: Sign a DPA with every processor
steps.body: List the suppliers that handle personal data for you, check what each agreement covers and set a review date.

steps.title: Check your transfers
steps.body: For every processor or recipient outside the EEA, record the country, the mechanism and your assessment.

starter.title: Check data that leaves the EEA
starter.body: Mark each processor whose data leaves the EEA. Full adds a transfers sheet for the country, the mechanism and your assessment.

steps.title: Decide how long you keep data
steps.body: Agree a period for each kind of record, then set the matching retention rules in each sheet's settings. Due records come to Workspace admin › Retention for approval.

starter.title: Decide how long you keep data
starter.body: Write the retention period on each record of processing, then set the matching retention rules in each sheet’s settings. Full adds a retention schedule.

steps.title: Be ready for requests from people
steps.body: Open the form "Submit a data subject request", check its questions, write its privacy notice and tell the people who receive requests where to log them.

steps.title: Be ready for breaches
steps.body: Open the form "Report a personal data breach", name a breach lead and tell everyone to report at once, however small.

steps.title: Assess high-risk processing
steps.body: Every processing record marked "DPIA needed" gets an approved DPIA with the DPO's advice.

steps.title: Mark the GDPR articles that apply
steps.body: In the GDPR requirements library, mark each article applicable or not, with a reason, and set its implementation status.
